Use Chrome DevTools to generate timeline events". dart2js developer_patch.dart reports Timeline events via performance.mark/measure.

Flutter 3.47.2 object.dart:1137-1187 flushLayout: `if (!kReleaseMode) FlutterTimeline.startSync('LAYOUT$_debugRootSuffixForTimelineEventNames')`, then `child.flushLayout()` inside that span; flushPaint same (1293-1335). Suffix ' (root)' when `_debugParent == null` (1698); adoptChild sets the parent `if (!kReleaseMode)` (1764), so in profile the child's plain LAYOUT/PAINT nest inside the (root) one. framework.dart:3087 BUILD under !kReleaseMode. Round 3 sentence matches.

ui-performance: "For example, if a frame occasionally takes 10 times longer than usual to render, it will likely be dropped, causing the animation to appear jerky." Jank is defined per frame ("each frame must render approximately every 16ms"), so an occasional long frame stutters regardless of the average. The page does not discuss averages explicitly.

Round 2: lesson section 4 now reads "When a change for speed makes code harder to read, make it only where such a recording shows a slow frame: a change that costs readability with no measured gain is a pure cost.", matching the ledger. best-practices: "If your frames are rendering in well under 16ms total in profile mode, you likely don't have to worry about performance even if some performance pitfalls apply".

best-practices, 'Control build() cost': "When `setState()` is called on a `State` object, all descendent widgets rebuild. Therefore, localize the `setState()` call to the part of the subtree whose UI actually needs to change." Separate advice for layout (intrinsic pass) and paint (saveLayer, Opacity, clipping). Supports 'too much time in BUILD calls for rebuilding fewer widgets' as one example fix.
